data.content_ref: inline:This conjecture contradicts the edge-construction enrichment programme shared by SRC_004, SRC_006, SRC_007, and SRC_011: any enrichment that injects new attack edges before the fixpoint changes the graph on which the grounded extension is computed, so the resulting labels are the skeptical extension of a strict supergraph, not of the admitted graph, and the claim that reinstatement 'remains derived' is vacuously true at best — the derived labeling is a function of injected edges, not of the admitted evidence. REFUTED IF one exhibits an admitted graph G and a polynomial-time enrichment E such that the grounded extension of E(G) restricted to G's vertices equals the grounded extension of G on every node for all admitted G — that is, if any enrichment is label-invariant on every admitted graph, then the contradiction dissolves and the programme is sound.
